turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I beg your pardon, ma'am, but I don't know if I should call anyone just now. My sister would have my head if I made a disturbance.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will call Estella at once, and you will not think of your sister's disapproval, for it is of no consequence to me what your sister may think.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: If it's not too much trouble, ma'am, I will go and call Estella, but I must do it quietly, so I don't make a noise in the house.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: Estella, I wish to see you at once. Bring your music, and come to my chair.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure if I should disturb Miss Havisham with the noise of my footsteps, ma'am, but I'll do my best to be quiet

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will bring Estella at once, and I will not be kept waiting. Do not dawdle, boy.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'll go, ma'am, right away, and I'll make sure to be extra quiet, so I don't disturb you or Miss Estella.

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: What is the meaning of this tedium? I have summoned Estella, and I demand that you bring her to me at once!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm not sure, ma'am, if I can go and find Miss Estella right away, as I don't know where she is, and I don't want to keep you waiting if I'm not able to find her

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will find Estella in the garden, I daresay. I will not be kept waiting by your ineptitude.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't think I should go and find Miss Estella right now, as I'm not supposed to leave my sister and my brother at home on their own

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: I will not be swayed by your petty excuses, boy. You will find Estella and bring her to me, or suffer the consequences.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't think it's right for me to be leaving my sister and brother, as they're very young and might get into trouble

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You dare to question my orders, boy? I will not be disobeyed!

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't think it's quite right for me to be playing with Miss Estella when my sister and brother are at home all alone

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You shall not concern yourself with the well-being of your sister and brother, boy. They are of no consequence to me, and you will do as I command.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't know if I can do that, as I'm not sure where Miss Estella is, and I wouldn't want to bring her here if she's not expecting it

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You are a foolish boy, to question my authority and my intentions. I will not be disobeyed.

turns.speaker: Pip
turns.text: I'm afraid, ma'am, I don't know if I'm worthy of playing with Miss Estella, and I wouldn't want to trouble you with my company if I'm not good enough

turns.speaker: Miss Havisham
turns.text: You will play with Estella, and you will do it now. I will not be denied.

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: Mr. Pumblechook’s boy, ma’am. Come—to play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Come nearer; let me look at you. Come close.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Look at me. You are not afraid of a woman who has never seen the sun since you were born?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: Do you know what I touch here?

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I am tired. I want diversion, and I have done with men and women. Play.

opening.speaker: Miss Havisham
opening.text: I sometimes have sick fancies, and I have a sick fancy that I want to see some play. There, there!

opening.speaker: Pip
opening.text: No, ma’am, I am very sorry for you, and very sorry I can’t play just now. If you complain of me I shall get into trouble with my sister, so I would do it if I could; but it’s so new here, and so strange, and so fine,—and melancholy—.
